definitions.explanation: Sesame seeds that have been dry-roasted to bring out their nutty flavor and aroma. A ubiquitous condiment and garnish in Japanese cooking.

examples.japanese: サラダに{炒|い}りごまをかける。
examples.english: To sprinkle toasted sesame seeds on a salad.

examples.japanese: {炒|い}りごまを{擂|す}り{鉢|ばち}ですると、{香|かお}りが{良|よ}くなる。
examples.english: Grinding toasted sesame in a mortar brings out the aroma.

examples.japanese: ほうれん{草|そう}の{胡麻|ごま}{和|あ}えには、{炒|い}りごまをたっぷり{使|つか}う。
examples.english: For spinach with sesame dressing, use plenty of toasted sesame seeds.

notes:
A compound of {炒|い}り (roasted, from {炒|い}る 'to roast/parch') and ごま ({胡麻|ごま}, sesame). Sold in small bags at any Japanese supermarket and used as a finishing garnish or as the base for sesame dressings and sauces.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {炒|い}りごまをふる: to sprinkle toasted sesame seeds
- {炒|い}りごまを{擂|す}る: to grind toasted sesame seeds
- {白|しろ}{炒|い}りごま: toasted white sesame
- {黒|くろ}{炒|い}りごま: toasted black sesame

RELATED WORDS:
- すりごま: ground sesame — pre-ground toasted sesame, sold in packages
- {練|ね}りごま: sesame paste — smooth paste made from sesame seeds
- {白|しろ}ごま: white sesame seeds — the most common variety
- {黒|くろ}ごま: black sesame seeds — stronger flavor, used in sweets and as garnish
- {胡麻|ごま}: sesame — the general term

USAGE:
{炒|い}りごま is the most common form of sesame sold for home cooking. It appears in countless Japanese dishes: {胡麻|ごま}{和|あ}え (sesame-dressed vegetables), きんぴら (braised root vegetables), {冷|ひ}やし{中華|ちゅうか} (cold noodles), rice balls, and more.
